g1|variants|copy control.summary: Copy control defines how data flows between sales, delivery, and billing documents in SAP S/4HANA Order-to-Cash. Variants differ by document level (header, item, schedule line) and whether they drive standard billing, intercompany billing, debit/credit memos, or returns.

g1|core|copy control|standard sales orde.title: Copy Control from Sales Order to Outbound Delivery
g1|core|copy control|standard sales orde.story: When a customer places an order, the warehouse needs to know what to pack and ship without retyping all the information. In SAP, copy control acts as an invisible copier that safely copies data from the sales order (OR) into the outbound delivery (LF) while following specific business rules.
g1|core|copy control|standard sales orde.why_business_needs_it: Automated copy control eliminates manual data entry errors, ensures legal and commercial consistency between the order and the shipping documents, and maintains the required document flow for auditing. Without correct copy control configuration, sales orders cannot generate outbound deliveries, bringing fulfillment to a complete halt.

modules.role: Defines copy control rules between source sales document OR and target delivery document LF at both header and item levels.
modules.hands_off_to: LE (Logistics Execution) to create outbound deliveries and execute picking and packing based on copied data.

modules.role: Consumes the copied sales order data to generate outbound deliveries, plan shipments, and execute warehouse execution steps.
modules.hands_off_to: FI (Financial Accounting) and MM (Materials Management) during goods issue for inventory reduction and accounting postings.

g1|core|copy control|outbound delivery t.title: Copy Control from Outbound Delivery to Billing Document
g1|core|copy control|outbound delivery t.story: Imagine a magical conveyor belt that takes a packed box ready for shipping and instantly turns it into an invoice asking the customer to pay, without anyone having to type the numbers all over again. Technically, copy control is the configuration framework in SAP S/4HANA that dictates how header and item data are transferred from a source document, such as an Outbound Delivery, to a target document, such as a Billing Document.
g1|core|copy control|outbound delivery t.why_business_needs_it: The business needs robust copy control to ensure that invoicing precisely matches what was delivered without manual data re-entry, preventing billing errors and accelerating cash collection. It maintains compliance and auditability by enforcing rules on which fields can be copied, recalculated, or updated.

modules.role: Defines copy control rules between delivery types and billing types, handling pricing redetermination and status updates.
modules.hands_off_to: FI-AR (Financial Accounting - Accounts Receivable) to post billing documents into customer open items.

modules.role: Receives billing data to post journal entries, generate revenue accounts, and manage customer receivables.
modules.hands_off_to: CO (Controlling) for profitability analysis and cost-center accounting.

g1|core|copy control|sales order to bill.title: Copy Control: Sales Order to Billing Document (Order-Related)
g1|core|copy control|sales order to bill.story: Copy control is the digital conveyor belt that moves data from a sales order directly into a billing document without requiring a delivery step. In SAP S/4HANA, copy control rules dictate which fields copy over, how prices recalculate, and whether quantities accumulate correctly for order-related billing scenarios like service orders or milestone billing.
g1|core|copy control|sales order to bill.why_business_needs_it: Organizations require order-related billing copy control to invoice customers immediately for services or fixed-price orders that bypass physical shipments. Precise copy control rules ensure that billing documents retain mandatory reference links to sales orders, preventing revenue leakage and maintaining strict audit trails.

g1|core|copy control|intercompany billin.story:
Imagine a giant toy store network where one store sells a toy to a customer, but another store in a different country actually owns and ships the toy. In SAP, intercompany billing copy control is the magical rulebook that copies the exact details from the shipping document over to the internal bill sent between the two sister companies. Specifically, this procedure links outbound delivery type LF to intercompany invoice type IV at both the header and item levels. If this rulebook is missing or torn, the supplying company cannot legally charge the selling company for the goods it shipped.

This standard SAP S/4HANA Order-to-Cash (OTC) configuration governs the transfer of data, pricing types, and routine assignments when creating an intercompany invoice (IV) from an outbound delivery (LF). It ensures financial compliance and correct revenue recognition across company codes during intercompany sales execution.
g1|core|copy control|intercompany billin.why_business_needs_it: Multinational enterprises require automated intercompany invoicing to properly settle inventory transfers and margins between legally separate organizational units when fulfilling cross-company orders. Without precise copy control settings, intercompany invoices fail to generate, block month-end financial consolidations, and cause discrepancies in intercompany clearing accounts.

doc_flow.what: The initial sales order is created with a delivering plant belonging to a different company code than the sales organization, triggering intercompany requirements.
An outbound delivery document of type LF is generated from the sales order to execute picking, packing, and goods issue from the supplying plant.
Goods issue is posted against the outbound delivery, reducing inventory in the supplying plant and creating material value postings.
An intercompany invoice of type IV is created by copying data from delivery LF using header routine 019, item routine 012, and pricing type C.
The billing document automatically posts financial entries, debiting the intercompany clearing account for the ordering company code and crediting revenue for the supplying plant company code.
